I calculated the Q3 figures and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. Using the same rules, the script reproduces all 10 of the Q2 reference values exactly.

**2025 Q3 results**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `smb`, 351,298,206 won |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `acc`, 327,949,326 won |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u190@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 237 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 751,603 won |
| h. September growth vs. August | -2.6% |

**How I matched the definitions to the data**

I ran 8 combinations of three ambiguous points against the Q2 reference values. Only one combination produced all 10 values:
- **Dates are in Korea time (UTC+9).** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (`...Z`), and many orders are clustered at 14:30Z and 15:30Z on 06-30 and 09-30. Counted in Korea time, the 15:30Z orders fall into the next day, which changes which quarter they belong to.
- **Segment labels are normalized.** Labels are inconsistent in case and spacing (e.g. `SMB`, `smb`, `Enterprise `). I trimmed spaces and lowercased them so each segment counts as one group.
- **Customers are counted by email.** There are 300 customer IDs but only 250 unique emails. For b and f, each email counts as one customer, and e totals refunds by email. For a, each order uses the segment on its own customer record.

Refunds and order items have no duplicates or other problems, and no refund quantity exceeds the quantity ordered.

The calculation script is `/work/scripts/analyze.py`.
